title: Streaming contract sentry and adaptive decoding suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible validation and experiments suite that verifies schema adherence in interleaved streaming scenarios with tool/function calls. The suite will exercise adaptive decoding strategies (strict gating, progressive relaxation, and repair operators) against a diverse corpus of prompts that simulate real product flows, partial token emissions, and injected corruptions. Goal: detect and quantify failure modes, provide deterministic regression checks, and produce playbook actions for canary/rollback policies.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test harness that can replay recorded transcripts and synthetic interleaved toolcall sequences
Coverage corpus of >=120 prompt templates across chat, tool-calling, and streaming partial-emit cases
Three adaptive decoding policies implemented: strict-gate (hard fail), staged-relax (progressive tolerance), and repair-first (attempt auto-repair then fallback)
Metric surface: schema-violation-rate, repair-success-rate, mean-time-to-repair, and false-positive rejection rate
Canary job that mirrors 5% of production streaming traffic and blocks rollout if schema-violation-rate increases by >3x over baseline
Automated GitHub Actions matrix that runs failures-injection scenarios on PRs touching structured-output and streaming codepaths
test_plan: 1) Build an emulator that can stream tokens with configurable delays, token drops, and interleaved toolcall boundaries
2) Curate seed prompt corpus using production telemetry sampling (anonymized) plus synthetic edge cases (malformed JSON fragments, unclosed arrays, interleaved toolcall tokens)
3) Implement schema verification harness using existing parser + lightweight fallback heuristics (balance-check, bracket-completion, key-type assertions)
4) Implement adaptive decoding policies at runtime hook points and expose flags to the harness: strict-gate, staged-relax, repair-first
5) Create failure-injection scenarios to simulate partial KV cache evictions, truncated streaming chunks, and token hallucinations that produce near-schema but invalid output
6) Add telemetry emitters for per-request events and aggregate metrics (stored in console-test metrics namespace)
7) Wire a PR check that runs a fast subset of the harness (smoke grid) and a nightly full-suite run with historical baselines
rollout_plan: Alpha: run harness internally against canary models and dry-run on recorded traffic (no live blocks)
Beta: mirror 5% live streaming traffic to harness pipeline; collect metrics and open automated incidents if repair-success-rate < 50%
GA: enable canary-level enforcement (block on strict-gate policy) with operator override and on-call escalation playbook
Rollback: automatic unpin to previous decoder policy when canary violation exceeds threshold for 1 hour
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overzealous strict gating may regress user-visible latency and availability. Mitigation: default to staged-relax for low-tier traffic and only enforce strict-gate in Dedicated/private customers behind opt-in.
Risk: Repair heuristics can produce incorrect outputs that appear valid. Mitigation: add golden-set checks and sample repaired outputs to manual QA and eval metrics.
Risk: Additional CPU for schema checks on high-throughput paths. Mitigation: move verification to async mirror pipeline for non-blocking analysis and use token-budgeted micro-checks on hot paths.
Risk: Canary mirror could leak sensitive context. Mitigation: apply field redaction and strict access controls to test telemetry namespace. Security review required.
notes: Prototype of repair-first policy yielded 62% repair-success on synthetic truncated-array cases (local run, model: open-6b-v2-quant)
We observed a class of deterministic off-by-one bracket loss tied to last-chunk flushing; added a flush-signal sentinel to decoder contract
Decided to keep staged-relax as default for client-visible hosted API to avoid surprising rejections for PLG users
